$comment: Tool contract for the on-board agent capability layer. A model gets five tools: three for seeing, two for acting. Issuing a credential, arming it, revoking it and reading the audit log stay with the operator (root Basic) and are deliberately absent: a model that can mint its own authority is not sandboxed. Every tool below is also reachable from bin/adc-agent, which is the recommended path because it adds envelope pre-flight, the 8 Hz pulse train and an unconditional stop on every exit path.

transport.auth: header X-Agent-Cap: <32 hex> (issued by POST /api/agent/token, armed by the operator)

function.name: see
function.description: Look before acting, and again after any surprise. Returns vehicle state, this credential's envelope, and the current perception: detected objects with class, confidence, normalised box, lateral offset (-0.5 left to +0.5 right), area ratio and a near/mid/far range class, plus a one-line summary. Also reports frames_behind and age_ms so you can tell when the picture is stale. Do not invent state; if this call fails, stop.

returns.profile.reason: string, why the follow profile is in its current state (target_lost, disabled, agent_active, ...)
returns.actuation.ready: boolean; false means commands will be accepted but cannot reach the motors
returns.perception.objects: array of {cls, name, conf, box, center, lateral, area_ratio, range, in_path}, at most 12; objects_total carries the real count
returns.perception.summary: one-line natural-language summary, e.g. 'person left, near range, conf 0.87'

function.name: frame
function.description: Fetch the current camera image as JPEG. Use it when a single sentence of perception is not enough — reading a sign, judging an unusual obstacle, confirming that a person is really standing there. The image is the raw camera frame with no overlays; use the box coordinates from see() to reason about positions. Prefer b64=true when your runtime can only consume JSON.

b64.description: true returns {"seq","width","height","age_ms","jpeg_b64"}; false returns image/jpeg bytes with X-Frame-Seq headers.

max_bytes.description: Refuse frames larger than this (HTTP 413). Default 1048576.

returns.seq: frame sequence number; compare with perception.frame_seq from see()
returns.age_ms: milliseconds since the frame was captured

function.name: drive
function.description: Publish one bounded motion primitive: drive at v m/s with differential steer for ttl_ms. This is a lease, not a setting: it expires and the vehicle stops. Do not call this in a loop yourself; hand a plan to bin/adc-agent instead, which pulses at 8 Hz, pre-checks the envelope and always stops on exit.

v.description: Forward speed in m/s. Additionally capped by the credential's v_max, which is usually lower.

steer.description: Half the left/right wheel-speed difference in m/s; positive = left wheel faster = turn right. Yaw rate is approximately 2*steer / wheel_track.

ttl_ms.description: Lease duration. 300-500 is the sensible range at 5-8 Hz.

returns.traveled_m: metres consumed against the credential budget
returns.actuation: live | blocked; blocked means the command was accepted but an interlock refused it

function.name: stop
function.description: End motion and retire the arming. Use this at the end of every plan, and whenever the situation is unclear. Stopping is always allowed, even when the credential is not armed.

function.name: estop
function.description: Emergency stop. Stops, disarms, and forces the follow profile off on disk so a service restart cannot bring it back. Use when the vehicle does something you did not intend; a human must re-enable it before anything moves again.

error_codes.403: credential not armed, or missing scope
error_codes.409: profile disabled, fault latched, or distance budget exhausted
error_codes.422: argument outside the credential envelope or outside the control-layer hard cap
error_codes.429: more than 25 commands per second on one credential
error_codes.503: no MJPEG frame available (camera stopped, or YUYV pipeline)
